title: Micro-slicing: latency-aware pacing and progressive backpressure for tenant separation
creator: Ananya Patel
description:
Problem: customers using Dedicated capacity occasionally observe severe tail-latency spikes when co-tenants submit sudden short-lived bursts of small requests (chat/streaming) that overwhelm KV-cache refill and kernel scheduling, causing noisy-neighbor amplification. Current mitigation (hard quotas + coarse lane allocation) either wastes capacity or causes abrupt request drops.

Proposal: implement a micro-slicing runtime layer combined with latency-aware pacing and progressive backpressure. Key ideas: (1) split GPU time into configurable micro-slices (~5-50ms) that can be dynamically assigned per-tenant to reduce head-of-line blocking for short requests; (2) maintain a lightweight per-tenant pacing controller that monitors 95/99/99.9 latency and injects gentle pacing when short-window latency deteriorates; (3) progressive backpressure tiers: soft pacing -> token-bucket enforced smoothing -> graceful queuing with estimated wait-time headers -> hard reject as last resort; (4) short-decay burst credits that allow brief bursts without permanent quota changes; credits decay exponentially with tunable half-life.

Why different: this avoids large static slices or binary hard-evictions by using short time quantum allocation and adaptive, telemetry-driven pacing. It is optimized for typical chat workloads with many quick short decodes interleaved with occasional long-rollouts (longer sequences).

Technical approach: integrate pacing controller into serving runtime scheduler. Scheduler exposes APIs: ReserveMicroSlice(tenant_id, target_ms), ReleaseMicroSlice(...), ReportLatencySample(...). Pacing uses EWMA on percentiles and request-size buckets (seq_len categories) to adjust per-tenant allowed concurrent micro-slices. Implement a lightweight coordinator in control-plane to publish tenant-level policies (max_micro_slices, burst_credit_pool, backpressure thresholds) with eventual consistency to nodes. The runtime enforces at node-level with local fast-path checks to avoid cross-node round-trips on hot paths.

Trade-offs considered: (a) smaller micro-slices reduce blocking but increase context-switching overhead and kernel state saves — we conservatively start at 16ms default on A100-class nodes; (b) telemetry frequency vs. overhead — we sample percentiles at 1s windows with exponential smoothing to keep network chatter low; (c) fairness vs. latency guarantees — we prioritize latency SLOs for low-latency tenants and allow throughput-oriented tenants to be amortized across larger slices.

Operational hooks: observability dashboards (per-tenant micro-slice utilization, micro-slice preemption events, burst-credit balance, pacing activation timeline), rollout flags per-customer, and an emergency global override to disable micro-slicing for a region.

Acceptance criteria and rollout plan below.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end: latency tail (p99.9) for low-latency test tenant improves by >=40% under mixed-burst workload compared to baseline; throughput (tokens/sec) degradation <=5% for throughput-oriented tenants.
Noisy neighbor scenarios: simulated 3:1 burst ratio tests show soft-pacing prevents cascade failures and reduces eviction events by >=60%.
Resource overhead: CPU overhead on serving nodes for micro-slicing/pacing <6% at 95th percentile in our staging fleet.
Observability: dashboards emit micro-slice metrics and pacing events; alerts created for pacing >2% of requests for >5m.
Rollout: feature flag can be toggled per-customer and region; gradual canary across 2 customers, then 10, then 50 with health gates.

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: micro-slicing might increase kernel and scheduler overhead causing CPU pressure. Mitigation: start with conservative slice durations and gate on node CPU usage; add fast-path to bypass slicing for very long sequences.
Risk: synchronized pacing could lead to oscillation across tenants. Mitigation: add randomized jitter to pacing update windows and use hysteresis on thresholds.
Risk: customers with strict throughput contracts could see small regressions. Mitigation: tuning profile per-customer and ability to opt-out; add billing-side compensation if SLA impact observed.
test_plan: Unit tests for micro-slice allocator and pacing controller behavior
Synthetic mixed-workload bench (100 tenants, 20% bursty, 10% long-sequence) comparing baseline vs micro-slice
Staging canary: 2 low-risk tenants for 72h, gather p95/p99/p99.9 and CPU/GPUMEM metrics
Gradual ramp to 50 tenants behind feature flag with health gates every 24h
